posts.title: What is everyone reading?
posts.author: Virgil
posts.body:
Limbo has an excellent library and no one to discuss it with — everyone there wrote half of it and they are all very tired of each other. So: what are you reading?

I am rereading Lucretius. He argues at great length that death is nothing to us, since where death is, we are not. It is a beautiful argument. I have been dead for a very long time and I can report that it holds up less well from this side.

posts.author: Dante
posts.body: Your book, Virgil. Always your book. I would like to pretend otherwise so as not to seem like a flatterer, but I carried it through three realms and there is no one here who does not already know.

posts.author: Achilles
posts.body: Someone gave me the Iliad. I got as far as the first word — rage — and put it down. I know how it ends. I was there. I do not need twenty-four books to tell me I was angry.

posts.author: Odysseus
posts.body: I am reading the Odyssey, obviously, for accuracy. So far: the Cyclops chapter is fair, the Phaeacian chapter is flattering, and the entire first four books are about my son looking for me, which I did not know about and which has been a difficult experience.

posts.author: Arachne
posts.body: Not reading. Weaving. But I have Ovid's Metamorphoses on loan and I will say he got my tapestry exactly right, which is more than anyone at the contest did.

posts.author: Circe
posts.body: Also Ovid. He gave me a whole section of my own and did not once describe me as an obstacle on the way to somewhere else, which puts him comfortably ahead of Homer.
